key_insight: A modified quantum annealing eigensolver can estimate atomic magnetic dipole hyperfine constants, extending quantum hardware use beyond energies to observable-level spectroscopy.
engineering_relevance: This shows D-Wave hardware can support small-scale relativistic atomic-structure calculations, offering a potential hybrid route for benchmark quantum chemistry workflows.
method: Quantum Annealer Eigensolver (QAE) modified with zooming and sigma-annealing.
Floating-point encoding used to recover ground-state eigenvalues and eigenvectors of Dirac-Coulomb Hamiltonians.
CSF truncation applied for larger correlation spaces, keeping only dominant configurations.
evidence_signal: Hardware runs on the D-Wave QPU matched GRASP benchmark values at the chosen three-decimal precision for Li, Be, Na, and Mg test cases.
watch_item: The demonstrated accuracy is limited by small Hamiltonian sizes, CSF truncation, and a three-decimal precision cap, so scalability to larger atomic systems remains uncertain.
paper_title: Applications of quantum annealing to magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants: First results beyond energies for atoms
